clue.text: Had something to eat, drinking lager top, and did a runner!

indicators.note: drinking means the meal word swallows the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: had something to eat means fed, past tense of feed

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so lager gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone ate, drank the head off a lager, then skipped out without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts L, the top of 'lager', inside FED.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a runner is slang for leaving hurriedly, usually without paying, so it means took flight.

clue.text: The crew go to Edinburgh

definitions.meaning: a crew of workers or thugs is a band or squad
in Scots dialect, the speech of Edinburgh, the verb to go is said this way

explanation.walkthrough: 'to Edinburgh' signals a Scottish word: in Scots, to walk or go is to gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a band of workers, and in Scots dialect the verb meaning go has the same spelling.

clue.text: Headband

parts.note: read literally as a band around a head: the ring of light painted above a saint

explanation.walkthrough: Not a sweatband: the ring of light shown circling a saint's head in paintings is a band about the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing circle drawn over a holy figure's head is literally a band at the head.

clue.text: Nail a ticket up showing the language

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the run is read from bottom to top, backwards
showing means these words display a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone pins a ticket high on a board in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' reveals NAILATI across 'Nail a ticket'; 'up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in Italy and its neighbouring regions is a language.

clue.text: Stargazing after good cooking

indicators.note: after places the stargazing word following the letter for good

parts.note: stargazing is the study of the heavens, the science of the stars

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at the stars after a fine meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The art and science of fine food and its preparation is a matter of cooking.

clue.text: Comment on a nice case of rivalry

parts.note: nice means agreeable or pleasant

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A remark about a friendly instance of competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes the first and last letters of 'rivalry', R and Y; 'on' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite, light remark made in conversation is a courteous comment.

clue.text: Unusual delay for a long drink

indicators.note: unusual signals that these letters are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd hold-up before someone gets a tall drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges the nine letters of DELAY FOR A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall trumpet-shaped glass holding about three pints, drained in one go as a pub challenge, is a long drink.

clue.text: The ground level is noisy, that's the drawback

indicators.note: is noisy means the word is heard spoken rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the ground level of a building is its floor

explanation.surface: Complaint that the downstairs is loud, which is the snag.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech FLOOR and FLAW are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect or weakness is a drawback.

clue.text: Stop everybody going under the trees

indicators.note: in a down clue, going under places the everybody word below the trees word

parts.note: a mass of trees is a forest
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Someone halts a crowd heading beneath the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent or head off something in advance, so to stop it.

clue.text: One takes the lead in chase and arrest

parts.note: to dog someone is to chase or follow them
to collar someone is police slang to arrest them

explanation.surface: Someone leads a pursuit and an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the lead' is not about leading: a collar on a pet is what the lead clips to, and the cleric's band carries the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap round a pet's neck is the thing a leash is attached to.

clue.text: Policeman who could manage to drop tail

indicators.note: drop tail means the last letter of the managing word is taken off

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: An officer who might get by if they lose their pursuer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop tail' removes the last letter from COPE; 'who' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop is informal for a police officer.

clue.text: Tear off at speed

indicators.note: off signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone races away quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TEAR; 'at' is a link word. 'Tear off' looks like a phrasal verb for dashing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a pace or speed of movement.

clue.text: Money talks with this creature

indicators.note: talks means the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: The saying money talks, with a hint at an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money talks' is the familiar saying; here 'talks' says the slang word for money is heard aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A female deer or rabbit is a creature.

clue.text: Dangerous food that should be dropped!

definitions.text: Dangerous food that should be dropped!

parts.words: Dangerous food that should be dropped!
parts.note: read literally, a scorching tuber you would let fall; figuratively, a touchy issue nobody wants to handle

explanation.walkthrough: A hot potato is an awkward issue to be passed on fast, as if it burned the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A controversial matter everyone wants to avoid is likened to scalding food you would quickly let go of.

clue.text: Disturbance in east coast port — sailor on a floor inside!

parts.note: Hull is a port on England's east coast in Yorkshire
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: inside means the middle of floor, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Uproar in a Yorkshire port as a seaman stands on the deck indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' takes the inside of 'floor', LOO; 'in' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar or commotion is a disturbance.

clue.text: Happen it's a printer's error!

indicators.note: an error suggests the letters have been printed in a wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A slip in printing just occurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges A PRINTERS; here the 's of 'printer's' supplies an S. 'it's' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire, in modern use, is to occur or come about.

clue.text: Hospitality that's nothing to write home about?

parts.note: O, shaped like zero, means nothing
to pen is to write
a house is a home

explanation.surface: Welcome that is nothing to write home about, nothing remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing to write home about' is the idiom for something unremarkable; 'that's', 'to' and 'about' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an open house means welcoming all visitors freely, a form of hospitality.

clue.text: Quiet old English brogue

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A soft, old-fashioned English accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brogue' looks like an accent, as in an Irish brogue; it is the sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a stout leather footwear style with punched decoration.

clue.text: Brightened up after being found not guilty

definitions.meaning: said of the weather or sky, brightened up means became clear
a defendant found not guilty has been acquitted of the charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'after being' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Skies that brighten have become clear, and an acquitted defendant has had their name freed of blame.

clue.text: Model soldier shot before noon

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a shot at something is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A perfect soldier is shot before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a gun firing; it is a try, a go. 'before' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Poorly rated company for artistic movement

indicators.note: poorly signals the letters are in a sick, disordered state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly reviewed firm sponsors an art style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' rearranges RATED into ARTDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco was a 1920s and 1930s design style of bold geometric forms, an artistic movement.

clue.text: Service in ship by master

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree
SS, steamship, prefixes a ship's name

explanation.surface: A church service held on board a ship, led by the captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'by' are link words. 'master' suggests a ship's captain but gives MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass is the celebration of the Eucharist, a church service.

clue.text: Polo is a rough game

definitions.meaning: polo is a sport played on ponies, so literally play on a mount
rough game means boisterous, rowdy fooling about

explanation.walkthrough: Polo is cryptically play on mounts; the phrase also means rough-and-tumble fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is sport on mounts, and rowdy boisterous fun is also called by the same two-word phrase.

clue.text: The energy required to exercise quietly

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
P, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: The stamina needed for gentle workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required to' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pep is liveliness and vigour, energy.

clue.text: Voting system that has nothing in favour of it!

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
O, shaped like zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An electoral method with nothing to recommend it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'it' are link words; the surface suggests nothing in favour, but the letter O is the nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro means for, supporting something.

clue.text: Higher degree student — one from the country

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a higher degree
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A postgraduate is one of the students from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner because British learner drivers display an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African nation.

clue.text: A less than amorous advance in the subway!

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten
to make a pass is to make an amorous advance

explanation.surface: A half-hearted romantic overture made in an underground passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' and 'in' are link words. In British English a subway is a pedestrian tunnel under a road, not a train system.
explanation.definitionFit: A British subway is a pedestrian tunnel beneath a road, which is a passage running below.

clue.text: Unusual end to war — a run on energy

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken from war

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A remarkable finish to a war followed by a rush on power.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means seldom found, uncommon.

clue.text: In the morning before the doctor's rounds

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: In the morning before the doctor goes on their ward visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like a doctor's ward visits; it means rounds of ammunition. 'before' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds of ammunition, bullets or shells, are informally called ammo.

clue.text: Dispatched some perfume to the audience

indicators.note: to the audience means as heard by listeners, a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: Someone posts a bottle of fragrance to the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent means posted or dispatched.

clue.text: Loving god returned, and was angry

indicators.note: returned means the god's name is read back to front

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Cupid came back in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses EROS; 'and was' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore in informal use means annoyed or resentful.

clue.text: Tempers can be lost in this feature of the landscape

indicators.note: be lost signals the letters lose their order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tempers may fray on this steep stretch of country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be lost' rearranges TEMPERS CAN; 'in this' are link words. 'Tempers can be lost' reads as an idiom about anger.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope or cliff, a landform.
